verdict.rationale: Navan advertises "unlimited policy and approval workflows" and its MCP/AI layer can explain which policy applies, why a transaction was flagged, and who must approve it, implying a rules engine with per-transaction policy limits (e.g., rideshare, hotel price caps). However, the evidence never explicitly describes configuring limits by category/role/context or confirms that in-policy spend auto-approves while only exceptions route to a human. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of policy-builder granularity (category/role/context), explicit auto-approval behavior for in-policy expenses, and independent/hands-on confirmation of the approval-routing logic.
